O best of gods, I create this, I swallow this, and I sustain this.
Just as a spider swallows and also emits threads,
even so, O best of gods, is this web of the world by you.
I am Time, whose food is the Brahmins and Kshatriyas, and who has Death as his foot;
having entered the individual soul (jīva), I abide within all beings.
He dwells eternally within the inner cave of the heart of all beings;
he transcends the qualities of all the senses and is devoid of all the senses.
These worlds have me as their support, and you, O gods and asuras, are the ones to be perceived within them;
I am the heater in the sun and the one who bestows grace in the moon.
In the wind I am motion; in fire I am indeed heat;
in Indra and Yama I am majesty; and in the Lord of Wealth I am prosperity.
I am the medicine even for the Aśvins; I am always the mother of the Maruts;
I am the heart of the Viśvedevas, and I always dwell within the hearts of the Vasus.
The Asuras and Suras are established in the state of *sāttvika* prosperity;
the Munis are characterized by *tamas*, while the Suras are characterized by *rajas*.
O wise ones, I am the three qualities, yet I am devoid of qualities and absolute;
for I am truly the qualityless one, established beyond the darkness of ignorance.
Likewise, I am the essence of the waters; I am the light of lights.
In the elemental ether, I am the conscious perceiver and the all-pervading source of sound.
Likewise, fragrance is the quality residing in the earth, and the gods are established therein;
I am Vāyu, and the gods are the primary creations of these [elements] (or, according to another reading: the conjunctions and disjunctions of these).
This world, consisting of the moving and the unmoving, the stationary and the sentient, has been described; their creations proceed according to the natural order of succession.
When these exist in reverse order, they are designated as dissolution;
O gods, in the performance of their activity, I have no part whatsoever.
The Nīlimpas do not exist through disappearance; rather, the eternal Witness exists. In the absence of my presence, the world would not shine at all.
Just as iron needles move in various ways when in the proximity of a magnet, so too do the gods and this world act under the influence of the Divine.
Today, all my playthings are at my disposal;
yet, for you, it is exceedingly difficult to truly recognize my true form.
I am free from the six waves and devoid of the fivefold functions;
yet as Brahmā, I alone create this world through the quality of passion (rajas).
Abiding in the quality of goodness (sattva), I am Viṣṇu, the protector;
and becoming Rudra, abiding in the quality of darkness (tamas), I withdraw all that is moving and unmoving.
I am Sadāśiva, the Lord of Gods; indeed, I am the one who bestows grace.
Assuming the form of Īśvara, I cause even those deluded by my māyā to be so.
I am intent upon the fivefold action, yet I transcend the five sheaths;
I am devoid of the five vital breaths, yet I move as one with the five elements.
This is my supreme power, consisting of delusion and obscuration,
by which you have been utterly infatuated, along with the world of gods, demons, and humans.
Whether stationary or moving, O Indra of the gods, this is my supreme power;
indeed, she alone is the cause of creation, preservation, and destruction.
This very power of mine is supreme, bestowing manifold knowledge;
O gods, bow down quickly to her, for by her grace [all shall be attained].
O gods, by my grace, the destruction of the power of obscuration occurs for you embodied beings as long as the ripening of karma persists.
And that power persists for the sake of distraction, O best of beings;
it is indeed a portion of myself, the individual soul (jīva), which expands through its own ignorance.
For, remaining unbroken within bodies of various origins, he experiences a share of suffering;
thus, in two ways, he dwells like a bird within the tree of the body-house.
One indeed experiences the fruit consisting of action—the pleasure and pain—while the other shines like a witness; thus it is according to the mantra, "Two birds [on one tree]."
O dwellers of heaven, it is Brahman alone who wanders through saṃsāra due to its own ignorance;
indeed, it is liberated by its own knowledge and by austerity alone.
Having fallen into a state of pride, one who partakes of the fruits of pleasure and pain always revolves indeed between heaven and hell.
One attains liberation through my knowledge, and not otherwise, even by millions of ritual acts;
this [body] dies when abandoned by the living soul (jīva), but the soul, O gods, does not die.
O best of beings, I am free from the six waves of affliction and reside within all bodies;
having entered this body consisting of the six sheaths, I am the illuminator of everything. (33)
With the six waves, the objects of the senses, and the six groups [of mental states], I desire the moving and the unmoving;
and being one whose will is true, I create all the worlds through my resolve.
By my mere resolve, the ancestors and the gods attend upon me here;
for me there is no grief, nor delusion, nor hunger, nor thirst.
For I am bodiless within bodies that are unstable;
I am the Great One, I am the All-pervading One, and indeed I am the indestructible Self.
I am beyond the three states, I am the unattached Puruṣa;
I am the all-pervading space, the light of all, the abode of all—I am the Lord.
He who knows me knows this; he who, deluded by ignorance, would give me away, would thereby give away this [world]. But having known the Bliss, one does not fear.
He attains supreme peace and, being steadfast, he no longer possesses desire.
Brahmā knows me; indeed, both gods and asuras know me as Brahman.
"He who knows me as 'Brahman exists,' for him I am the deliverer;
I am neither inwardly cognitive nor outwardly cognitive, for I am Brahman."
This internal self is indeed always immortal, yet it appears in the form of death;
I alone am eternally Brahman, devoid of the distinctions of witness and witnessed.

This self is eternally Brahman; though situated in space and time, I am that very reality, according to the uniform meaning of such scriptural statements as "Thou art That" and "All this is the Self."
I alone am the illuminator within all words;
having realized supreme bliss, one indeed crosses the ocean of worldly existence.
Having recognized me as the one to be worshipped, one crosses over both grief and delusion;
you should know me alone, for everything else is indeed in vain.

I am truth, knowledge, and infinite; from my truth comes the truth of the world—[the reading is "from untruth comes the truth of the world"]. Indeed, by my very existence, the inert, manifold world becomes conscious.
Indeed, the entire world is but a spray from the ocean of Great Bliss; I am the essence within all beings, though only those who recognize that essence truly know me.
O Asuras, those tastes and even mere joy always sustain you;
O Asuras, who else could ever live perpetually without the intoxicating sky?
Neither does the mind go there, nor do the senses;
I am indeed the Supreme Self today, and he is today that very same Śvaka.
It is indeed unattached, without the touch of speed, and without smell; it is indeed devoid of scent. It is without hands, feet, or functions, and is devoid of the anus, genitals, and so forth.
Indeed, I alone am devoid of both means of knowledge and objects of knowledge, far beyond the reach of logic;
I know everything, yet no one knows me. (50)
I have made the sense-organs turn outward; therefore, one does not see me. Only someone endowed with my grace truly knows me, or perhaps even he does not.
I am the seer, devoid of the seen, and I alone am the act of seeing;
O best of gods, I am the sixteenth [tattva], and I alone am the hearer and the smeller.
I am the Lord, the knower of the intellect and the mind, as well as the life-force of the vital breath;
indeed, I alone am all the faculties within the body and the senses themselves.
All dissolve into me alone; I am not established in them—[the reading is "nāhaṃ teṣvavasthitaḥ"]. I am indeed the one, non-dual, the fourth, Śiva himself. (54)
Wine, wrestling, intoxication, the world, the pierced, and the gods—these always exist;
I am the ground, the supreme bliss, and no one knows me.
(Verse 190) I alone am he who moves at will through the world of the insentient and the sentient; indeed, no manifold universe exists, for whatever appears is merely like a thirst for the path.
Therefore, there are no mountains, no earth, and no hosts of gods; indeed, nothing at all exists in this world.
O gods, everything shines as Śambhu; to whom else does this entire universe belong? 56.
Thus ends the fifty-first chapter, titled "The Exposition of the Essence of the Vedas," in the first part of the Śrī Śivarahasya.
The Fifty-second Chapter, titled "The Purification of the Devas.
Īśvara said:
"I am that which is both eternal and non-eternal; I alone am indeed Brahman and non-Brahman."
Indeed, [it extends] to the east, to me, and to the west, as well as to the south and the north.
I am the worlds below and above, and I am the cardinal and intermediate directions;
I am the male and the neuter, and I am the female and all the deities.
I am neither female nor male, nor indeed am I eternal;
for I am bodiless within bodies, and unperishing amidst all that perishes.
I alone am the light of lights, the eternal and imperishable self-luminosity;
I am within fire, wind, sun, moon, and all beings.
Living beings do not know me, for I am indeed the source of all beings;
I alone am the beginning of the Vedic meters, and I alone am the Gārhapatya fire.
I am the Dakṣiṇāgni and the Āhavanīya fire; I am Truth, I am the Cow, and I am the Suras.
I am the Cow, I am the Most Excellent, I am the Youngest, and I am the Eternal.
For my speech, O lords of the gods, consists of the Ṛg, Yajur, Sāma, and Atharva Vedas;
I am the imperishable, I am the perishable, I am the secret, and likewise the Puṣkara.
I am subtler than the subtle, O gods, and likewise greater than the great;
I am the Lord with eyes on all sides and arms on all sides.
O gods, I, whose head is the universe and whose feet are the universe, who possess a thousand eyes and a thousand feet,
now transcend this entire world of ten directions.
I am the Lord of immortality, the inner Person within all;
having removed the skull-caps of all, I stand established within them.
This person within me has golden hair;
indeed, I am swifter than thought, and by me this entire world is pervaded.
In the end, it dissolves into me alone; there is nothing whatsoever other than me.
I am indeed without breath, without mind, pure, and devoid of senses. || 12 ||
I am neither wise, nor unwise, nor indeed possessed of both kinds of wisdom;
for while all beings sleep, O gods, I remain perpetually awake.
I am indeed the unmanifest Lord, yet manifest, abiding in the hearts of beings;
I am the pillar, devoid of qualities, and free from both cause and effect.
I am indeed the Supreme Self, devoid of the perishable, the imperishable, and so forth;
and I am neither day nor night, neither being nor non-being, but Sadāśiva.
If it were possible to wrap up the expanse of space in a fold,
then, having failed to recognize me, there would be an end to your suffering.
I am the one to be known by all the Vedas; I abide as the essence within the Upanishads.
Indeed, I alone am the one in my own glory; I am the supreme subject of the Upanishads.
I am indeed the primordial sound of the Vedas; I am the eternal Praṇava.
I consist of the three morae beginning with the Praṇava, and I am the essence of all mantras.
I consist of the five syllables and am free from the five great sins;
I am without attachment, nor indeed do I have any attachment, for I am indeed the universe itself.
He who transcends the universe, whose abode is the universe, who is superior to the universe, the Lord of Umā;
all of you are the bound souls (paśus), and I am your Lord.
"O best of gods, through my grace, you must now strive for liberation; my knowledge arising from the words of the Vedas is one thing, while other arts are another."
O gods, through both knowledge and ignorance, I, who am Brahman itself, transmigrate;
being liberated, I indeed liberate all, including the asuras and humans.
O gods and asuras, I am not to be obtained even by hearing through [ordinary] actions;
even while hearing, O best of ascetics, some do not find me at all.
"O wise ones, it is certain that this entire world is afflicted by this;
how do you regard it? Please tell me. (24)
This manifestation of mine which has been described cannot be known otherwise than through faith;
this knowledge born of the Vedānta scriptures must not be imparted to one whose mind lacks trust.
By giving [this away], one falls into hell together with one's ancestors;
this essence of all the Upaniṣads has been proclaimed by me.
Now, for you, I shall correctly provide this very [instruction] which severs the knot of the heart;
but it is certainly not for one who is not a disciple, nor for one who lacks devotion, nor for one who has no son.
O best of gods, one should give this to the ascetics who belong to Śambhu;
O foremost of deities, for him, liberation is attained without effort.
"O gods, by my grace, liberation shall be held in the hands of all those who have observed the Śirovratam; to them this [merit] must be granted."
"O gods, this 'Head Vow' was indeed performed by me in ancient times;
having taken up the sacred ash with the mantra beginning with 'Agni', one should touch the limbs."
O gods, this vow bestows liberation from the bonds of the individual soul;
for it is through faith, austerity, and the worship of my linga that the gods [attain their state].
A man who wears the triple mark of ashes on his neck becomes liberated from sin;
and by the repetition of the five-syllabled mantra, there is the destruction of the five sins.
O best of gods, [the merit comes] from the meditation and recitation of the Rudra hymns especially at the root of a bilva tree, and from dwelling constantly in my sacred fields.
And because they dwell in the Unliberated (Avimukta), at the very end there, through the dissolution of the body,
the gods likewise [attain liberation] by means of meditation upon my form accompanied by Umā.
This very supreme knowledge is obtained through my grace;
O gods, knowledge is not obtained otherwise than through ritual action and worship.

This, the essence of all essences, the core extracted from the web of the Vedas, has been told; it is the sole cause for the destruction of all ignorance. O gods, this primordial knowledge that pierces the heart must not be imparted to foolish mortals in this world.

The destruction of births throughout hundreds of existences and the lamp of the path to liberation—indeed, [this state] free from the torments of sins arising from hundreds of misdeeds—is thus attainable through meditation on the excellent worship of me, the Giver of Boons; it is difficult to reach even through the supreme enlightenment of the teachers or the words of the Vedas. (37)
(Verse 192) O gods! Tell me, what is your prowess? Hari, Hara, the one seated on the lotus (Brahmā), Indra, the Sun and Moon, Wind and Fire, the Maruts, the Viśvedevas, and the two Aśvins;
the Vasus, the hosts of Ādityas, the Ṛbhus, the hosts of Maruts, and you, Kubera and the others—speak!
Therefore, I shall observe their strengths and weaknesses; let them show me their prowess with respect.

Skanda— Having heard these words of Śaṅkara, Hari, Hara, and the lords of the thirty gods, surrounded by the host of deities, beheld that supreme greatness and, oh, the manifestation [of the Lord] before them.
With their minds filled with pride, the hosts of gods bowed to Śiva and said:
"Now hear the words arising from him regarding each of our respective duties that produce sovereignty."
Brahmā said:
"I create the manifold world, including gods, humans, and gandharvas, as well as oceans, mountains, caves, rivers, streams, and forests."

O Śambhu, I, whose mouth is graced by Your favor, respond to the one beginning with "namas-tasmai" and ending with "asurādyakaḥ"; I am one for whom the web of the Vedas has been fully mastered. || 40 ||
Viṣṇu:

"Indeed, having cut off the discus-wheels of many preeminent Daityas and torn them apart in battle, I protect this entire universe of moving and unmoving beings; O Lord, it is my conviction that there is no one equal to me. (41)
Rudra:
At the end, the ocean—greater than even the dissolution—is covered by the stream clinging to the excellent tip at the root of my trident;
this entire universe, with its moving and unmoving beings, enters my mouth and I devour it like a swarm of insects on fruit; this is my desire. (42)
Indra—
seated upon the temples of the rutting lord of elephants stationed in the triple heaven,
encircled by the girdle of the gods, and radiant with a manifest crest-jewel—
I am Indra, whose lotus-feet rest upon the surface of the earth and who holds the thunderbolt in his hand. || 43 ||
The Lord, whose wrath is directed against enemies headed by Vṛtra and Urajaṃbhaka, has drunk the excellent Soma; indeed, no other god has ever done so. 44.
Vāyu said: "To me, all the worlds appear as unstable as the wind, with their rivers, streams, and mountains moving at will, and the oceans surging most restlessly."
He whose mighty wind causes the rows of great trees to fall, who always dwells with the gods and Maruts, and who resides within the bodies of the foremost among men; || 45 ||
Sūrya: With my intensely fierce orb and the masses of my rays, I [dry up] the drops of water from the breasts of the world’s clouds, which have arisen from the excessive rains of the great deluge.
From the rising of the sun until its setting, I indeed nourish the entire world with renowned seeds, grains, and other provisions by way of the path beginning with light. || 46 ||
Agni—
illumined by hundreds of flames, bestowing satisfaction upon the hosts of gods, well-established in sacrifices and other rites, and providing the *kavya* offerings to the hosts of ancestors;
Standing at the mouth of the great ocean, I am the one whose crest has well-cooked the essence [of the sacrifice],
and I am your forehead-eye who has purified the three worlds.
Yama:
I am indeed Yama, the remover of the pride of the multitude of hells for those who possess sin; wielding a most fierce staff, I am truly impartial toward all.
Obeisance to you, who have bestowed your gaze upon the feet of Śiva; by the cries of my terrified soldiers, the sins wandering in the world flee away out of fear. 48.
Kubera:
Impelled by you, I, the lord of Yakṣas, who have attained friendship with your lotus-feet, nourish those destitute of wealth with riches.
With its syllables rising up, the lord of the eight musical scales celebrated;
what is this answer? My mind is thus inclined toward him alone. (49)
Candra: I am Soma; I am the friend who causes the lotus-thicket of your face to blossom, and I am the sweetness and luster residing in the mass of matted hair shimmering upon your crest.
"O Lord, today I nourish the multitude of plants, for I am now established in Your light; and today my left eye has become a vessel for Your grace—please grant me peace this day. (50)
Varuṇa—the lord of the waters; the master of the oceans, rivers, streams, and the boundless sea;
whose banner shines brightly; the radiant lord of the Gaṅgā that flows beyond the shore.
May that worship of Your feet—which creates a snare for those who produce demerit, yet is frequented by the best of assemblies, and which removes worldly existence—be mine alone. 51.
All the gods— the Viśvedevas, the Aśvins, and all the Maruts together with Indra— drink the Soma by your command,
O Lord, Master of the Pramathas, who are intent upon the protection of the worlds. 52.
Sūta said:
Having heard these words of the hosts of gods, Śambhu—under whom the celestial tree has bowed—spoke to the deities;
for he felt a joy arising from their lack of decorum upon perceiving even their speech to be of such noble form.
Īśvara:
This man, appearing like a blade of grass, has been fashioned by me through my resolve; O best of gods, quickly instill within him the essence of your own majesty.
"I see all this as your grace; O gods, may you cross over [this danger] quickly.
Having spoken thus, this Lord of the Universe was indeed quickly concealed by Umā. (54)

Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Hara, the Lord of the Immortals (Indra), Yama, Vāyu, Agni, Sūrya, Kāśa, Candra, Īśāna, Vasu, Varuṇa, and Vitteśa—the guardians of the quarters—then stood with their excellent weapons and powers over that man of straw. (p. 195)
Then you were neither able nor powerless to move even the slightest bit. || 55 ||
Accompanied by the Goddess and endowed with a multitude of virtues, the hosts of gods— whose crowns were bowed low through the radiance of their intense devotion— sought refuge in Hara with fervor;
led by the Lord of the Daughter of the Ocean (Viṣṇu), they all praised him perfectly from every side.
The Lord of All, the Sovereign of the World, the Great Lord Śiva, who is to be worshipped by the three worlds.
To create, protect, or consume; to burn with exceeding power, dry up, bind, or move the entire rod of punishment, or even to flood it with water;
and to fill it with the rays born of the moon through their fortunes—the gods were not masters of these things.
Then, with faces bowed in shame, they took refuge at the feet of Maheśa with devotion. || 57 ||
Thus ends the fifty-second chapter, titled "The Purification of the Gods," in the first part of the Śrī Śivarahasya.
The fifty-third chapter, titled "The Devotion of the Goddess Praised by the Gods.
Jaigīṣavya said:
"I have heard this most wonderful narrative and the life-story of Śaṅkara."
When the Lord had vanished from sight, what did those best of gods do? || 1 ||
O Śikhidhvaja, salutations be unto you; tell me that in detail, for I am not satiated by the stream flowing from the nectar of your mouth.
And upon hearing it again and again, a greater desire arises. || 3 ||
Sūta: Having heard these words of Śambhu, that six-faced one [Kārttikeya],
while the hosts of Gaṇas and the gods were listening, [spoke] to the lord of sages.
Having addressed those brahmins, he then spoke of the deeds of the God.
The Prince: Listen, O Sage, to the supreme and noble life-story of Dhūrjaṭi;
thereafter, all those beginning with Brahmā and Viṣṇu, along with Indra and all the hosts of Maruts, [will appear].
The suns, moons, and Varuṇas praised that Umā, the Mother of the World, whose form is the essence of compassion and who is adorned with beautiful ornaments.
With their palms joined in reverence, they all then meditated upon Śivā.
The Gods:

O Daughter of the Mountain, who gladdens and delights, who provides diversion to the universe, O you who are praised by Nandin! O Dweller upon the peak of the Vindhya, the best of mountains, O Playful Consort of Śambhu, O You who are lauded by Viṣṇu! (9)
Victory, victory to you, O crusher of the demon Mahiṣāsura! O daughter of the mountain with your beautiful matted locks!
O Blessed One, O wife of the blue-throated Lord Śiva! O bestower of immeasurable prosperity upon your devotees! || 10 ||
Victory, victory to you, O Daughter of the Mountain, who dispelled the dust from Dhūmravilocana’s eyes with a mere *huṃ* sound;
victory, victory to you, O crusher of the demon Mahiṣāsura, O lady of beautiful braided hair! 11.
O you who are like a creeper of blood-seeds arising from the blood-seeds dried upon the battlefield;
O you who have gratified the multitudes of bhūtas and piśācas with the great offerings of Śumbha and Niśumbha! 12.
Victory, victory to you, O crusher of the demon Mahiṣāsura! O daughter of the mountain with your beautiful matted locks!
O Mother of the Universe, who delight in dwelling in the fragrant groves of Kadamba trees and who take pleasure in the celestial abode! 13.
To Him who dwells within His own home, the lofty mansion of the Himalaya—the crest-jewel of mountains;
to Him who is sweet as honey and who was praised by Brahmā with great agitation upon the threat posed by Madhu and Kaiṭabha.
Victory, victory to you, O crusher of the demon Mahiṣāsura, O goddess with beautiful matted hair, daughter of the mountain!
You who possess a voice as deep as the rumbling of clouds, who subdue the unassailable, who delight the ill-mannered, and who take pleasure in nourishing [your devotees]. 15.

O nourisher of the three worlds, O delighter of Śaṅkara, O defiler of sins, O one who delights in the cowherd settlements; O witherer of the race of demons, O one who restrains the arrogance of the wicked, O nourisher of the virtuous, O bearer of the lion! 16.
Victory, victory to you, O crusher of the demon Mahiṣāsura, O daughter of the mountain with your beautiful matted locks!
Your waistband of arrows is clearly visible as they repeatedly touch the string of your bow at every moment.

On the shore of the battlefield, which was the arena for the clash of fourfold armies—where hosts of excellent warriors with golden-brown quivers and speckled arrows were slain, resembling the host of the gods. || 18 ||
Victory, victory to you, O crusher of the demon Mahiṣāsura! O daughter of the mountain with your beautiful matted locks!
O you who have subdued the multitude of elephants with their trunks by rending the crest of the peacock! 19.

O Lord of Beasts, whose fierce prowess is renowned for tearing apart the formidable Bhaṇḍa who had seized the temples of the enemy's elephants; O Lord of fierce warriors, who has quelled the haughty enemies by splitting their heads with the staffs of your own arms! 20.
Victory, victory to you, O crusher of the demon Mahiṣāsura, O goddess with beautiful matted hair, daughter of the mountain! (21)

Victory, victory to the Goddess, the savior of the royal lineage of the Lord of Nagas! You who are resplendent with ornaments upon your breasts, gait, hips, face, neck, belly, waist, thighs, hands, and arms; you who resemble a water-laden cloud, a mountain, an elephant, a sandbank, the moon, a conch, a palm, a lion, a plantain stalk, a red lotus, and a lotus fiber; you whose neck is secured by a necklace of pure star-like pearls; you with bimba-red lips and eyebrows fashioned like the crescent moon of the eighth day; you whose earrings form circles like the sun and the moon; and you who are illuminated by a pearl-ornament on your nose that resembles a rising cluster of stars.
Protect, protect those deluded by your māyā who are adorned with all ornaments! || 22 ||
Having thus offered praise and prostrated themselves on the ground like a staff, all those gods,
with their hands joined in reverence upon their heads, then spoke as follows.
The gods said:
"We have all been deluded by you; we do not know Maheśvara, who is equal to all the gods and the cause of all causes."
He is the Lord of lords and the Consciousness of all conscious beings;
because of separation from Him alone, everything here before us has become as mere straw. (25)
O Maheśvarī, O Mother, although we are capable in the tasks of creating and destroying the world, we are indeed unable to do even the slightest thing; therefore, we have always sought refuge in you.
Salutations to you, O Mother of the World; be ever gracious toward us.
By you all this is pervaded, and by you the universe is sustained.
At the end, all that consists of gods, asuras, and humans dissolves into you alone;
you are the Supreme Goddess Śakti, who shares half the body of Maheśa.
O Śivā, by your grace may the delusion of all be destroyed;
you are the power (Śakti) rooted everywhere, while Maheśvara is the wielder of that power (Māyī).
"We have all sought refuge in you, yet we have been deluded by your māyā.
Having spoken thus, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and the others prostrated themselves on the ground like a staff.
Then, having risen, they all beheld her in the midst of the sky,
shining like a streak of lightning situated within a dark rain-cloud.
Resembling molten gold, adorned with all ornaments, wearing a crown bound with the crescent moon, and possessing a countenance equal to the moon’s radiance. (32)
Having seen her, whose eyes reached to the corners of blue lotuses and who was beautiful with a pure form, they bowed again to the Goddess and cried out, "Protect us! Protect us!"
Having heard the words of the gods, Umā then spoke to the deities in a speech that was bold, firm, and sweet, which destroyed their ignorance.
The Goddess said:

"This is Brahman, this is the Self, situated in the state of the Praṇava, devoid of the measurer, the means of measurement, and so forth; I am indeed the wielder of Māyā, and here, O gods, I am Śakti."

Worship that Great Lord, the sovereign of all, the possessor of power, who, though subject to Prakṛti, created this diverse universe; he who is the source of the origin and destruction of the universe and the remover of all worldly existence. || 35 ||

Since indeed Hari, Brahmā, Rudra, Indra, and the others were born from Him, and since they surely abide within Him—by you this entire web of worlds has been pervaded; therefore, take refuge in the Lord and worship Maheśa. (p. 198) 36.
I am that power by whom, through the grace of Bhava, this entire universe is made to appear as a mere sport;
seek refuge in my very power, which alone grants liberation from worldly existence. (37)
For that Śiva, the eternal, the ever-pure, the ancient one, there is neither effect nor instrument;
yet you, O lords of creatures, are deluded by his Māyā, and it is through separation from him alone that all this [world] exists in such a manner.

The comparison with a blade of grass would be in vain; therefore, all you gods, quickly worship Rudra Īśāna, who dwells within the heart of space, who is desired by all, and who has withdrawn from all the senses. || 39 ||
Having spoken thus, that Mother of the World vanished from the sight of the gods.
Hearing what the Goddess had said, all the deities then stood with palms joined in reverence.
With their limbs adorned with divine splendors and beautified by the triple-ash mark (tripuṇḍra),
the gods performed the Pāśupata vow and offered worship to the Liṅga.
Those who are ever devoted to the five-syllabled mantra, diligently reciting the Rudrādhyāya for a year while remaining absorbed in meditation upon the Five-faced One;
Without even seeing Mahādeva or the Mother of the worlds,
they raised their arms and praised Īśāna, the Supreme Lord.
With single-minded devotion, the gods, with their hands joined in añjali,
[praised him] with the fierce Ṛk and Sāman verses, as well as those found in the Ātharvaśiras.
The Goddess said:

O You whose sword is intent upon those devoted to the *praṇava*, who destroy fear, and who are an ocean consisting solely of the essence of merit— we, the multitude of speakers, take refuge in Your name, which is the word to be expressed by all, and which serves as the helmsman for the ocean of worldly existence that leads to liberation.
The first verse of the Rigveda, "tvām agnim īḷe," designates you as Agni; the other [verse] mentioned in the Veda speaks of you as splendor and vigor.
These [verses], moreover, declare you—the Lord, the unsurpassed master of the soma-juices—to be Agni, the cause of protection, according to the Samaveda.
O Lord, whose body consists of water, you who are Śambhu, manifest through the eight forms revealed by the speech of the Atharva Veda;
when it comes to describing your formless nature and qualities, the four Vedas—with their great primary branches and sub-branches—cease to function.
With devotion, they praise the Blessed One—who transcends both speech and mind—with eightfold bodies.
Thus ends the fifty-third chapter, titled "The Hymn to the Goddess by the Gods," in the first part of the Śrī Śivarahasya.
Chapter Fifty-Four: The Devotionally Praised Secret Doctrine of the Gods (Devakṛtopaniṣatstuti). The Gods:
"He who is Rudra is indeed the Blessed Lord; and he who is Brahmā—to him indeed be salutation after salutation!"
Salutations again and again to him who is indeed Rudra, who is the Blessed One, and who is Viṣṇu. || 1 ||
Salutations again and again to him who is Rudra, the Blessed One; and to that Rudra, salutations again and again.
Salutations again and again to him who is Rudra, the Blessed One; and to Umā, salutations again and again. || 2 ||
Salutations again and again to him who is indeed Rudra, the Blessed One, and who is Vināyaka; salutations again and again to him who is indeed Rudra, the Blessed One, and who is Skanda. || 3 ||
He who is Rudra is indeed the Blessed One; he who is Indra, to him indeed be salutation after salutation!
He who is Rudra is indeed the Blessed One; he who is Agni, to him indeed be salutation after salutation! || 4 ||
He who is Rudra is indeed the Blessed One, and he who is Vāyu—to him indeed be salutation after salutation!
He who is Rudra is indeed the Blessed One, and he who is Sūrya—to him indeed be salutation after salutation! || 5 ||
He who is Rudra is indeed the Blessed One, and he who is Varuṇa—to him indeed be salutation after salutation!
He who is Rudra is indeed the Blessed One, and he who is Yama—to him indeed be salutation after salutation! || 6 ||
Salutations again and again to him who is indeed Rudra, the Blessed One, and who is Nirṛti; salutations again and again to him who is indeed Rudra, the Blessed One, and who is Īśāna. || 7 ||

Salutations again and again to him who is indeed Rudra, the Blessed One, and who is Kubera; salutations again and again to him who is indeed Rudra, the Blessed One, and who is the constellations. || 8 ||
Salutations again and again to him who is Rudra, the Blessed One, and who is the eight planets; salutations again and again to him who is Rudra, the Blessed One, and who is the sages. || 9 ||
Salutations again and again to him who is Rudra, the Blessed One, and who is the eight Vasus; salutations again and again to him who is Rudra, the Blessed One, and who is the twelve Ādityas. || 10 ||

Salutations again and again to him who is indeed Rudra, the Blessed One, and who is the eleven Rudras; salutations again and again to him who is indeed Rudra, the Blessed One, and who is the earth. || 11 ||
He who is Rudra is indeed the Blessed One, and he who is Water—to him indeed be salutation after salutation!
(pṛ0 200) He who is Rudra is indeed the Blessed One, and he who is Fire—to him indeed be salutation after salutation! || 12 ||
Salutations again and again to him who is indeed Rudra, the Blessed One, and who is Vāyu; salutations again and again to him who is indeed Rudra, the Blessed One, and who is Ākāśa. || 13 ||
Salutations again and again to him who is indeed Rudra, the Blessed One, and who is Bhūḥ; salutations again and again to him who is indeed Rudra, the Blessed One, and who is Bhuvaḥ. || 14 ||
Salutations again and again to him who is Rudra and who is Bhagavān, and to him who is Sva;
salutations again and again to him who is Rudra and who is Bhagavān, and to him who is Mahas. || 15 ||

Salutations again and again to him who is Rudra and who is the Blessed One, and to him who is the people; salutations again and again to him who is Rudra and who is the Blessed One, and to him who is austerity. || 16 ||

Salutations again and again to him who is indeed Rudra, the Blessed One, and who is Truth; salutations again and again to him who is indeed Rudra, the Blessed One, and who is the vital breaths. || 17 ||
Salutations again and again to him who is indeed Rudra, the Blessed One, and who is the mind; salutations again and again to him who is indeed Rudra, the Blessed One, and who is everything. || 18 ||
Salutation again and again to him who is Rudra, the Blessed One, and who is Time; salutation again and again to him who is Rudra, the Blessed One, and who is Death. || 19 ||
To him who is indeed Rudra, the Blessed One, and who is the past—to him indeed be salutation after salutation!
To him who is indeed Rudra, the Blessed One, and who is the future—to him indeed be salutation after salutation! || 20 ||
Salutation after salutation indeed to him who is Rudra, who is the Blessed One, and who is the present; Om at the beginning and at the end, and the threefold utterance of Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ. || 21 ||

You are indeed Brahman; you are the threefold upward path, the goal, nourishment, and Maheśvara. You are the universe and that which transcends the universe; you are the oblation and the great oblation.
He is the done and the undone, these [worlds] and the supreme goal;
indeed, he is the progenitor of Nārāyaṇa and others, as well as of Aryaman and Varuṇa.
You are the progenitor of Vāyu, the great lord of heaven and earth;
you alone are indeed the Lord of all, the witness of all, and everything itself.
You are ungraspable among all beings, transcending the qualities of all the senses;
you are without marks, yet you possess a body, being all-pervading and eternal.
O Mahādeva, all the gods worship you as Vāmana;
O Śambhu, the world is born from you, it abides in you alone, and it dissolves into you.
Nothing exists as separate from you; in the ultimate sense, nothing is distinct [from you]. || 27 ||
(Verse 28) You are the one unborn who, delighting in her, remains close to Māyā—the unborn, who is red, white, and black, and who gives birth to many beings of similar form;
yet you, the unborn, abandon her once she has been enjoyed for her pleasures.
One should know Māyā as Prakṛti and the Great Lord (Maheśvara) as the wielder of Māyā;
by the parts produced from you, this entire world is pervaded.
Indeed, there is nothing here that is not manifold; for everything is presided over by you alone.
Yet, the dull-witted, disregarding you, fancies himself to have accomplished all his goals.
"O Śambhu, we fools were ignorant of the world beyond; deprived solely of you, we are not even capable of moving a blade of grass. You alone are our refuge and our supreme goal. (31)
This entire world is pervaded by you; who indeed, being bereft of you, could perceive what is deficient?
You alone are Rudra, the creator of all, transcending the universe, and the supreme perceiver.
The Self transcends all beings, beyond the sheaths, higher than the highest;
O Lord, you alone are the great devourer, and death is your condiment.
O Lord of Beings, the world of Brahmins and Kshatriyas is your rice-offering;
you are the tail of Brahman, the foundation, peace, and the imperishable itself.
All deities reside in the heart; they are established in the vital breath within the heart.
You are the Puruṣa in the heart; you consist of the three measures and that which is beyond them.
You are the syllable Oṃ, the Praṇava, the all-pervading, the infinite, and possessed of infinite prowess;
you are the Savior, the Subtle, the Radiant One, the White, who dwells within every body.
You are Īśāna, the Blessed Lord Rudra, Mahādeva, and the Sovereign;
you are the Supreme Brahman, the Supreme Abode, the Ultimate Shore, and the Final Goal.
You are the hero, the valiant one, the person, the abode of all beings, the universal one, the Lord of the universe, the giver of life, and the imperishable Self.
You are the eye of the eye, the very ear, O Lord; you are the mind of the mind and the knower of the intellect. 38.
You are the lord of lords, and we are indeed your cattle; O God, you thus protect us and likewise consume us.
Everything originates from you, O Lord; you alone are one, yet you appear as many through the illusory power (māyā) of the Supreme Person.

Oil in sesame seeds, clarified butter in curds, water in streams, and fire in wood—in this same way, O Great Lord, all is strung upon You, the non-dual; that which is born from You, that which belongs to You, and that which is consumed by You—all this is indeed You alone.
Qualities, actions, and the like do not exist; nor do name, form, or power, for You are distinct from the power of knowledge.
Abiding in the heart, You are the past and the future, the ancient, the one Hero, known solely through the qualities of the Vedas. 41.
O Maheśa, you are the form of the primordial sound *oṃ* and the nature of the creator; you are the one to be sought as a boon, as well as the subtle atom.
You are the Great One, the conqueror, the one who has conquered, and indeed the unconquered. You are the space within the cloud, the ether, and the syllable *ka*. You alone are all this.
O Radiant One, Sovereign Lord, whose abode is the source of all existence, You alone are the father, the mother, and the brother, knowable as the Supreme;
You are the remover of ailments, the physician free from sin, the handless and footless Self, devoid of all change.
O Lord, You alone are the supreme light, manifesting by Yourself; there is no other deity more powerful or more beloved than You.
You are neither day nor night; You are the Sovereign, the ultimate limit, and the Lord whose eyes behold all things. (44)
Neither the Vedāntas nor the Vedas have encompassed your knowledge, which has indeed been realized by you through the mind alone today;
even the ether, the earth, the water, the wind, and the fire, as well as the entire manifest universe, are yours.
You are the leader of the universe, the sustainer of the universe, and its Lord; through your knowledge, one may find everything here.
Through your ignorance, all are deluded; by your grace, we have been awakened by Ambā.

The Supreme Self, beyond all states, you alone are; you alone are Brahman, appearing in the form of the transmigrating soul. You are free from sorrow, free from death, without grasping, without thirst, bodiless, undecaying, and ancient.
You are the eternal Law (*ṛta*), the Truth (*satya*), transcending name and form; for who indeed can know this immeasurable form of Yours?
O Great Lord, You are the Supreme within the imperishable syllable (*akṣara*) of the *ṛc* verses; there is nothing else besides You from which this afflicted world could have come into being.
The seer does not see anything other than seeing; you are the witness of vision, devoid of the expressed and the expression, and so forth.
You alone are the Great Lord, the single primordial sound, the sovereign of knowledge; O Lord, you alone are he whom the Veda knows.

Salutations to you, O Hara; salutations to your radiant heat; salutations to you, O flame! O God of gods, sovereign of the universe, Śaṅkara, known through the Vedas—let your other weapons of terrible form consume others, but may you be auspicious toward your devotees; O Śambhu, slay our enemies with your trident!

O Śambhu, you who traverse this entire universe offering oblations, the first among us, whose vision is sight and who are seated upon the lotus of the mind; grant us blessings and wealth. You are the creator of all, visible through the mind, the ordainer and the dispenser, whose supreme form is beyond perception.
Through the worship of your feet, they obtain all their desired objects; there is indeed no doubt in this matter.
You are our mother, you are our father, and our initiator; you are our mother, our kinsman, and indeed our supreme teacher.

You are renowned among the gods by this very name; indeed, you alone are this Rudra. Though the ancient seers sought to know you, O Śambhu, even the modern ones find you inscrutable; for this entire world, with its impurities and merits, is afflicted by you alone.
This entire web of beings has indeed been emitted by you; yet no one knows you as you truly are, for the deluded perceive you through a distorted vision.
Shrouded by the mist of *māyā*, those born of the scriptures—who on earth would be satisfied with their own lives and enjoy worldly pleasures? 54.
Through sacrifices, gifts, and those desiring their desires, you are beyond heaven and beyond the earth, O Child;
you were the primordial city of the gods and asuras, and you are the majesty of all beings in the form of the Embryo. || 55 ||
(Verse 203) Who knows you, who are devoid of the multitude of beings, in whom the Lord—the universe—is dissolved within the Vedas?
O Unborn One, this wondrous world is placed within your navel; you alone are that in which the entire universe and the worlds reside.
Then the Gandharvas and Oṣadhīśa as well, O Śambhu, bow to you with all their senses and their minds;
the wise ones who meditate upon Brahman worship you, beholding you with their hearts and minds.
The gods do not perceive you as such, hidden and dwelling within them;
you are the eye of the universe, with faces and arms everywhere, the Lord of the universe, and the protector of this world. 58.
Heaven and earth shine from You alone; the sun blazes in the sky with its rays, and Soma with its lunar mansions and planets.
Others, devoid of devotion to You, do not know this; for they have not sought refuge in You, the unborn Lord. || 59 ||
Skanda:
Having thus offered praise, all those most excellent of gods prostrated themselves like staffs before the Supreme Self; the hosts of deities beheld him.
To Mahādeva, the eternal mass of splendor situated in the sky. || 61 ||
Having worshipped Bala with excellent bilva leaves, he [approached] the one whose feet are honored by the intense splendor of the submarine fire and the foremost of great serpents,
and who is fond of the Bāṇa-liṅga worshipped by the son of Bali.
Śiva, the subduer of Bala, the enemy of Bali and Bala, worshipped by Bāṇa,
marked by the jewel on the hood of the serpent dwelling in the cave, whose lotus-like hand is adorned [by the serpent],
and who bears the crescent moon bowed down by gods and asuras of exceeding strength.
The gods beheld Hari, whose excellent limbs were held firm, as he discharged his excellent arrows.
Thus ends the fifty-fourth chapter, titled "The Hymn of the Upaniṣads Performed by the Devas," in the first part of the Śrī Śivarahasya.
The fifty-fifth chapter, titled "The Exposition of the Devyupaniṣad.
Skanda said: Then the gods [beheld] Mahādeva, the eternal one, situated in the sky.
[He saw] the God, accompanied by Umā, the bestower of boons, charming with a gentle smile. || 1 ||
His neck was adorned with a beautiful garland of blossoming *hallaka* flowers,
and the faces of the quarters were illuminated by the rays of the moon’s sharp beams.
His body possesses a dense radiance like that of an autumn cloud as clear as a crystal casket;
his face is beautified by three eyes and adorned with serpent-earrings rising from it. (3)
His face is adorned with earrings shining from the hoods of Kuṇḍalīśa;
his head is drenched by the Gaṅgā, the crescent moon bound upon the slope of his matted locks. (4)
He was captivating, with hands like those of a young deer marked by the stainless *śūla* [weapon],
a great-souled one who dwells in all directions and is adorned with jeweled bracelets.
He was resplendent with a sword fastened to his broad hip, which was covered with a black antelope skin,
and was accompanied by the Goddess, whose lovely face shone with a gentle smile.

She possessed the fragrance of the finest lotuses mingled with the scent of *dhammilla* flowers and jasmine; her forehead was beautified by a tilaka of red lead, and she shone with the luster of pure jewels.
Adorned with various ornaments that bring singular splendor to each respective limb,
he destroys the pride of ten million Cupids and surpasses a hundred times ten million suns.
Although his body was emaciated and surpassed even ten million moons in brilliance, Śaṅkara,
the Great Lord, made a loud proclamation to those gods with a thunderous voice.
Then, gladdening them with his deep and sweet voice,
the Lord of the Pramathas, the friend of Śivā, spoke to those lords of the gods.
Īśvara:
O all you best of gods—Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara;
Yama, Anila, Anala, Bradhna, and Marut; Vāsava and the two Aśvins!
O gods— Sūrya, Candra, Indra, Varuṇa, and Dhanādhipa, the lords of the directions—
listen today to my supreme and beautiful speech.
For you,
who possess great prowess, have exerted every effort with all your power upon this man made of straw.
O gods, nothing at all arose that was capable of protecting the world,
nor of burning, creating, bestowing, consuming, or swiftly destroying it.
Now they are bereft of my splendor, dull-witted, and clinging to ego;
they are devoid of my power and compassion, and are currently powerless.
This supreme power known as Umā, who rests upon my lap,
is the one skilled in the creation, sustenance, and instruction of the universe.
The daughter of Dakṣa, the lord of mountains, was praised by the gods for her causal agency;
yet she has no cause nor any effect, for she is unborn and eternal.
Indeed, all of you know the manifold variety of her powers;
she is my supreme form, and in her absence, I [am nothing].
Nothing at all is to be done here, for I am indeed a non-doer and unattached;
I alone am without support, O gods, while this world has me as its support.
O gods, you are the cause; this Śivā is the one who creates the manifold world.
Through union with her power, I am empowered in every way.
My supreme power, which is beyond [all things], exists by its very nature;
some even say it is time, nature, necessity, or desire.
Likewise, the hosts of spirits and other sages are utterly deluded;
this entire world of moving and unmoving beings is the manifold manifestation of her power.
Bow down quickly to her, O gods, through her grace,
if you are indeed freed from the two powers of projection and concealment.
O best of gods, for as long as one is not liberated from the power of distraction, even after attaining my supreme knowledge, that duration is considered long.
However, you shall become free from obscurations and preeminent in compassion;
O virtuous ones, by my grace, your knowledge shall be complete in every respect.
O gods, as long as there is cyclic existence, may you who possess knowledge and hold authority attain that which arises from the Vedas and Vedānta.
"O gods, by the grace of the Goddess, supreme knowledge and sovereignty have been attained by me.
Then the gods, having heard the words of Śambhu according to their true meaning, [acted accordingly].
Falling to their knees upon the earth, the gods, with palms joined in devotion, praised the Mother of the World for the sake of obtaining the grace of the God of Gods.
O Goddess,
whose face is like the autumn moon, whose gait surpasses that of the lordly elephant, O Auspicious One,
whose radiant tresses resemble dark blue clouds and whose lower lip is like a beautiful bimba fruit!
O Śiva, whose eyes are like the petals of a blue lotus, whose compassion is profound, protect us today with mercy! 29.
O Śaṅkarī, whose lotus feet are bowed to by the hosts of gods, asuras, and sages;

O Maheśvarī, who rests upon the great lap of Maheśvara; O Bhavānī, whose braided hair is adorned with blooming mallikā flowers; O destroyer of worldly existence, who annihilates the multitude of sins of your green-clad devotees!
We bow to your lotus feet, which grant liberation alone. || 30 ||
To her who dwells in the Kadamba grove, who is fond of the luster of jewel-Kadamba flowers,
whose face and lips are as famous for their beauty as the full orb of the autumn moon,
and whose fragrant, most lovely, and well-formed lotus-like limbs—
To Heramba, whose curved cavern-like trunk has millions of blazing eyes at its tip. || 31 ||
O Daughter of the King of Nagas, who wears the crescent moon,
O Maheśvarī with beautiful cheeks, who utterly bewilders the hosts of asuras—
homage to your lotus-like feet, which shine upon the crowns of those with handsome faces.
[He is] the one who destroys the wrestler of sin, blazing from the crest-jewel of his most excellent crown.

O Śivā, O Goddess whose lotus feet are radiant as the refuge for the minds of noble people, you have made the range of the Kulācala mountains beautiful with your tilaka-mark, having shattered the multitude of sins that took refuge in those mountains out of fear of you. (Note: An alternative reading is *kulācalabhayāśrayāt*.)
Be gracious, O Śaṅkarī, whose lotus feet are bowed to by the winds and fires! 33.
Sūta said:
Having heard the praise of the gods, the Supreme Goddess was delighted;
being gracious, she spoke these profound and very sweet words to the gods.
The Goddess said:
"O gods, by your hymn of praise, I am pleased and have become well-disposed toward you;
O deities, I shall grant you everything desired—this very knowledge of Śiva."
O observer of noble vows, by means of this knowledge of the marrow, you shall attain supreme peace;
having abandoned the conceit of "I," you shall become a knower of the universal selfhood of Śiva.
You animals have been liberated through the majestic power of my illusory energy (māyā-śakti);
for I alone am the one to be worshipped by all, and I am indeed the object of meditation for everyone.

I am both consciousness and that which is existent and non-existent, and this entire universe is eternally fixed in me; for you are deluded by my māyā, while I alone am this coming into being and passing away.
I myself am giving this divine knowledge.
I alone cause the entire world to perceive; I move through all the Vasus, as well as through the Ādityas and the Viśvedevas.
I alone blow forth like the wind, setting all worlds in motion. 40.

I bestow wealth upon the one who offers oblations, upon the sacrificer who presses the soma for the sake of great heroic power. I am beyond the sky, I am beyond the earth; for I am the first and highest upon the earth. 41.
This is the Inner Controller, the immortal, the ancient one, who is eternally seated in the hearts of all people.
Wise men perceive this Self, hidden and entered within, by means of the heart and the mind. 42.
He is the Lord of Beings, He is the bridge, the supporter, so that the worlds may not be confounded.
While all things sleep, He remains awake, the Person fashioning every being. 43.
Within the sun, indeed, this immortal, golden Puruṣa is seen as Śiva;
he is the Ordainer, the Disposer, the Self-Ruler, the Sovereign, and the Lord of Creatures. || 44 ||
This divine God is the one ancient one, unattached among those who are attached, by virtue of qualities, names, and actions.
For this very self of beings, being established in every single being,
is seen as one and also as many, like the moon in water.
Just as the sun appears to move only because of the movement of the water, so too does this [Self] appear to move among all beings; yet it is not at all tainted by their qualities.
Without marks, possessing the same nature as space, he has no end, no beginning, and no middle;
pervading the world yet not the diverse world itself, he is the support of all, the one of wide strides, eternal.
Devoid of distinctions, this ancient poet is the independent, primordial Person;
hidden within the hidden, he is the one who has reached the further shore of the beyond, difficult to behold even by those perfected in yoga, and yet he is all-pervading.
O gods, although he dwells together with you,
none of you know him who shines eternally within the heart as the light of all that is manifested, yet remains devoid of the Great Bull.
(Verse 51) For I am indeed the very nature of this [Lord], yet the gods—who are ever partakers of suffering—do not know me.
Here I am the Goddess Light; I abide as the moon, the sun, the stars, the sages, and the supreme state of the planets.
And there is never for us any web of difference; for I am Māyā, while He is the Great Lord, the wielder of Māyā.
Śiva is indeed to be grasped through being, yet His nature is without a nest (foundation), the creator of both existence and non-existence.
Having perceived this Person, the knower of all arts, the adorable God, one attains ultimate peace.
This Self is to be seen through austerity (tapas), and not by other means; nor indeed is there any sign of it.
For him whose own self chooses its own body, there is the attainment of the grace of the Benefactor;
by the attainment of which no other gain does a person desire. O gods, this knowledge of his is difficult to comprehend.
The wise poets who know the past, having known this Great Lord, remain unshaken;
they cross over sorrow, whereas ordinary people do not—being constantly bound to the qualities (guṇas). (55) [Note: The reading "na jāyate" is interpreted as "na jānate" (they do not know).]

Likewise, he who is the support of the senses, whose form is immediate yet formless, who is both formless and the supreme ether, who dwells within the city [of the heart] amidst the manifold universes, and who is praised even by the multitudes of Vedāntins—[to him I bow]. || 56 ||
The essence of essences, most worthy of savoring yet beyond tasting, devoid of taste, well-guarded;
the fourth state, Indra, eternally risen, transcending qualities through its attributes, a drop of the divine abode. (57)
This is the infinite, the substratum of majesty, the Lord, the plenum, the limit, the essence—unique and without a second.
There is no other such majesty; He is the foundation, the Seer, the Primal One, this Self devoid of material flavor. 58.
He is Brahman; He alone is Indra; He is all that is moving and unmoving.
He is the Self, free from evil, stainless, sorrowless, deathless, without hunger, and without thirst. || 59 ||
For this Lord is one whose desire is truth, devoid of qualities, and possesses vast majesty;
he is bodiless, the creator of the universe, the master of all attributes, and the God who remains unshattered by those things that are shattered.
He is indeed free from passion, immortal, sorrowless, transcending grief, and devoid of the attributes of birth;
he is praised by the gods, the assemblies of Vedas, and the sages, for he is truly beyond the reach of the senses and beyond the scope of logic.
This Infinite One acts through the multitude of bodies, just as a spider emits a web of threads;
He blazes with radiant energy within the sun, and He is gratified by the sages through the multitude of sacrifices.
(Verse 63) He who protects Soma, the navel of immortality; he who transcends time and ever protects the universe;
there is not even an atom here that is distinct from him—he is this ancient Lord, my Sustainer.
This Self, the Great Lord, though formless yet possessing form, is blue-necked, pervaded by light, and eternal;
He is not slain when the body is slain, for He is the divine God, the ancient Deity.
Seeking that Brahman, they worship the supreme, peerless, auspicious Lord who transcends the faculties of intellect and senses;
He is neither one whose consciousness is within, nor one whose consciousness is without, nor one whose consciousness is both, and He is the most worthy of honor.

The creator of the universe, possessing manifold forms, the sole enveloper of the universe; hidden in the cave of the heart, dwelling in the depths, the ancient one, transcending all states, the primordial and singular Praṇava. 66.

I [behold] the Great One, the Supreme Self, the Lord, subtler than the subtle, who pervades this [universe]; shining resplendently among the multitudes of beings, unattached, transcending all limits, and self-luminous through His own radiance. (67)

Fools, imagining that the mere tip of a hair, established in the heart, is the reflection of the individual soul (jīvābhāsa), do not realize that this is neither the individual soul nor Śiva, the primordial creator; for there is nothing whatsoever higher than Him, nor anything else inferior.
The vast Brahman is pure, the eternal law, the truth, the Lord, supreme delight, the great knowledge, the one bliss.
Those who know this become immortal; others, however, enter only into suffering. 69.
This very one is supreme bliss; that bliss is Brahman, the ultimate.
Indeed, you gods and asuras are but mere portions of this bliss.
This alone is the supreme limit; this indeed is Brahmā, this is Śiva himself.
For it is this very one who is fashioned by the mantras arising from the network of Vedic mountains.
Having spoken thus while the gods were looking on,
that Mother of the World addressed the god Mahādeva, who is beginningless, unborn, and imperishable.
Skanda—
Thus, with their minds delighted by these words of the Mother, those gods were then further gladdened by various statements from the heads of the diverse Vedas.

Enveloped by streams of bliss, they behold that goddess Agajā, the beloved of the Lord of the Mountains, and the God surrounded [by his attendants] situated in the midst of the sky, perceived through the eyes of the Vedas.
Thus ends the fifty-fifth chapter, titled "The Exposition of the Devyupaniṣad," in the first part of the Śrīśivarahasya.
Chapter Fifty-Six: The Worship of the Field Created by the God.
Sūta said:
[One should worship] the Lord of Gods, who has the three worlds within his belly, seated upon a great bull, and accompanied by his attendants.
With palms joined in reverence, she was endowed with humility and possessed of qualities such as prudence and the like.
The large-eyed Great Goddess spoke to Virūpākṣa.
The Goddess said:

"O gods, by the grace of the Blessed One, this knowledge—which bestows the great purpose of the Mahābhārata—has indeed come to me alone. Today, through your satisfaction, my friends have achieved their goal; O hosts of gods, you have now attained the destruction of your enemies."

You are the beginningless Person, dwelling in the city [of the body], hidden in the cave, situated in the abyss; you are the ancient one, transcending the qualities, unattached among those things composed of the qualities, indestructible, the supreme Self, and the purifier.
There is no manifestation of difference other than You; there exists no poet, no wise man, no sovereign, and no self-born creator.
Nevertheless, You are the supreme Lokāyana (the Way of the World), for by means of those born of creation, You uphold bodies here in this world.

The all-pervading Great One, the sky, heaven, both worlds, and space—you are Rudra, the Lord, without a second. You are indeed the desireless one whose desires are fulfilled, the Infinite, the Limit, the divine God, the sole Seer.
O Maheśa, all these unborn and undecaying ones have sought refuge in your southern face of terrible form.
All these are bound by desire; therefore, you ought to sever their bonds this very day.

The renunciation of the ocean was indeed the one eternal among the eternals, the conscious among the conscious, and the Lord of lords; from you, O Lord of lightning, the guardians of the world came into being. (7)

O Śarva, you who transcend mind, speech, and intellect, the protector of all, the dwarfless among all, tawny, honey-colored, and reddish-brown, the leader of the universe; with thousands of rays, the planets attained delight. (8)
O Maheśa, these people, who are turned toward grace, should therefore be protected by you in the worlds;
through your sovereignty, let them have their desires fulfilled, for they have no other source than you among all things.
May they attain the yoga of supreme sovereignty and be liberated from my bonds of illusion and the like.
Skanda: Then, having heard the words of the Goddess, the Lord, the treasury of compassion, spoke to all the prostrate immortals, headed by Viṣṇu, Brahmā, and Indra.
Then Lord Umādhava, having joined his hands to his head, spoke to the gods with these words: "Indeed, let your power descend [upon him] now."

Īśvara: O best of gods, having been awakened by this Goddess, you have thus become those whose purpose is well-ascertained through the realization of Vedānta. By means of meditation on me, attain for a long time that knowledge which is difficult for the ignorant to obtain. (13)
This Self is not always visible in the sky even by the eye, nor by Vedic doctrines, nor by the logic of the scriptures;
I am to be perceived only through austerity, by the grace of the Guru and the grace of Śiva.
Indeed, your vast knots, established from time immemorial, are being severed; for who could know this to be so?
There is no future state for you children, who travel solely upon the path of the realm of beginningless ignorance.
O lords of the worlds, you have been appointed by me in this world for as long as the cycles of manifestation endure;
having attained knowledge, you shall become the lords of the gods among the powerful in every kalpa.
Follow me; today, through pure austerity alone, you shall be perfectly at peace.
Knowing this, those with distracted minds find no delight; therefore, Maheśa alone is to be praised by the Vedas.
Through sacrifices, gifts, austerity, fasting, and residence in my sacred field, they become free from the dust of worldly attachment;
wearing the triple-ash mark (tripuṇḍra), they are liberated from the bonds of existence by means of head-vows and mantras such as "Agni" and others.

With their bodies smeared with pure ashes, let them perform the recitation of the Raudra hymns for my delight—those who find joy in the repetition of the five-syllabled mantra and are satisfied merely by the worship of my linga. (19)

Free from hardships and devoted to me, the one pervaded by rays (Śipiviṣṭa), who am the manifest eightfold form, they worship me day after day with their cherished bilva fruits; having destroyed their delusion, they take delight in the intense state of liberation.

Meditating always upon me alone—who have entered the heart as the destroyer of all suffering and who abide within the heart—one attains that most difficult-to-attain knowledge which is the innermost treasure-chest, nourished by supreme contentment. (21)
Whatever you desire, even the slightest, offer it to the Three Heavens; being filled with joy, apply yourselves to that.
By that very means, may the unbroken knowledge you desire now bring about the destruction of the bonds of worldly existence.
"Out of affection for you, I joyfully bestow upon you today these eternal snares;
oh, have you forgotten that I entered into your very hearts so that my desires might be fulfilled even by you? (23)
I am full, yet I am indeed incomplete; being full, I am more than full, for there is nothing incomplete within me.
By the grace of the Goddess, let those whose desires are liberated wander about contented, possessing perfected accomplishments.
Nevertheless, I shall describe a small portion of that majesty which is difficult for me to express today, as it resides in the unmanifest:
among all the gods, he who is eternally and at all times in the form of a *liṅga* is seated upon the peak of the mountain. (25)
"In these places I am to be worshipped as the beginningless Lord; for you, beholding my form is exceedingly difficult to attain.
But I, the eternal one, established in the form of the Liṅga, am to be worshipped by you. (26)
That very *liṅga* is my *liṇga*; it cannot be known in this way, for it possesses the edge of a razor.
O gods, in the ultimate sense, I possess two forms; indeed, this entire universe consists of both that which has form and that which is formless.

This primordial Liṅga of mine—three-eyed, joined with the moon-crested Lord, accompanied by Ambā, and blue-throated—is indeed formless; yet through worship and other rites, it purifies the world (or, according to another reading, "it acts as the progenitor of the world").
Therefore, since that [state] is obtainable only through extreme hardship, you should seek refuge in Him;
for dwelling on Kailāsa is difficult for you to achieve, as my abode there is not always accessible to you.

O Lord, though I am the one who illumines everything, I dwell there eternally free from illusion, joined by Ambā and the hosts of Gaṇas; ever established within the Liṅgas of Kailāsa, I sport forever.
At Kedāra, Oṃkāra, and likewise at Avimukta, Mahālaya, Rudrakoṭi, and Prabhāsa;
on the Himālaya, situated at the peak of Śrīnaga, as well as in other regions where the Liṅga is well-established. || 31 ||
"Having worshipped [it], may they be liberated and free from fever; this secret has been told, O best of gods. (32)
Sūta said:
Having heard these words of the charming Girijā, Brahmā, Indra, and the others— Viṣṇu, Īśāna, the hosts of Maruts, along with Varuṇa— bowed down to Maheśa Śiva.

All the gods, who were worshippers of the Liṅga, having joyfully obtained from Śaṅkara the magnificent and great awakening of knowledge leading to liberation, departed for their desired destinations. (33)

On the supreme mountain of the Himalayas, Hari [worships] the Lord— who is as lovely as the matted locks of the daughter of the best of snowy mountains, which shimmer upon his head like a crown of snow and nectar—
with offerings of lotus-born flowers by means of the daughter of the ocean.
At the end of the day, he went to the excellent field of Surangaka.
Having attained the syllable *Oṃ*, the Lord of Bhāratī, standing on the banks of the Narmadā,
praised me, Umā, with flowers, offerings of bilva leaves, and mantras residing in the Vedas;
he thereby cast off all sins as well as the ignorance dwelling within his heart.
He praised the eightfold form [of Śiva] with his own mouths, which were intent upon the creation. || 35 ||

Rudra, having reached this Avimukta—the path of non-liberation and the abode of the Liṅga—along with the excellent Gaṅgā, [worships] you, Viśveśvara, the Lord of the three worlds, the granter of desires, Ambikā, and the daughter of the mountain with her very wide eyes. (36)

Having worshipped with heaps of flowers, sprinkled with the essence of milk and water, and honored with excellent bilva leaves, O Princess of the City, he then obtained that most pure and renowned knowledge of the Vedas, which is otherwise unattainable. (37)

Then Indra, having worshipped this very Lord Maheśvara— the one whose throat is beautiful with nectar— with excellent bilva leaves, became satisfied upon attaining that pure, ever-arisen, and undivided knowledge of mine which resides within the Vedas.
Yama also, having worshipped Śiva on the excellent mountain Gandhamādana, attained the state of hearing [the Vedas] through his own sins;
he then became liberated in heart by means of three-leaved bilva leaves offered to Śiva.
He alone is the sovereign lord of the most excellent southern quarter, the perfection of happiness. || 339 ||
O Umā, when the Lord of Śrīśaila is renowned during the evening twilight, the Lord of Wealth (Kubera), having worshipped Him and been freed from sin, attained knowledge that is invincible;
likewise, by resorting to the fortnight [of the lunar month] and beholding Him, one may obtain pure liberation. || 40 ||

Then the two Aśvins, having reached Karahaṭṭapura and worshipped Nāgeśa with various beautiful flowers, likewise attained liberation; and those two lords of physicians likewise obtained the Veda and long life, O Umā.
Vāyu, having worshipped the Lord of the forest at Kāmada-vaidyanātha with bilva fruits,
tender flowers, water, and food, quickly attained liberation; and Agni, indeed, having worshipped Puṣkareśvara, the sovereign of the three worlds.
O Mother, one who is liberated from sin is renowned as having consumed everything that arises from food. 42.
Having reached Gokarṇa, those Maruts indeed worshipped me, the venerable Lord; O Śivā, the Vasus praised me with *bilva* fruits and tender sprouts, and the sons of Diti likewise.
O Daughter of the Mountain, those twelve Ādityas also [worshipped] me, the glorious Tryambaka. (p. 213)
O Great Goddess, having offered oblations with the *homa* rites and worshipped the Rudras with three-lobed *bilva* leaves, || 43 ||

O Girijā, even the moon, though his orb is composed of matured nectar, attained liberation by worshipping Śambhu—who dwells within the exquisite white lotus of the heart-lotus—on Mount Gopa; and likewise, O Daughter of the Mountain, even the sun attained liberation by worshipping Śambhu there.
Having worshipped Hara at the foot of the single mango tree and Kāmākṣī with heaps of objects of enjoyment, the gods attained liberation— even those who were once intensely attached to Kāñcī.
Others as well— planets, sages, gods, asuras, and humans— did likewise.
The hosts of Gandharvas, Uragas, Yakṣas, and Rākṣasas, having honored me, were released. || 45 ||
In Śrīkaṇṭha, in Tṛṇaśaṅkara, in the well-established Ratnādri-mauli, in the son of the Mountain King who is the progenitor of the venerable Mothers, in the venerable Kālahasti-giri,
in the pair of banks of the Jambū-liṅga and Kaverī, as well as in Japya and Kumbhaka—
In the meritorious city of Śrīvedakābja, which is auspicious, white, upright, and the abode of the Vedas.
In the auspicious Śvetavana, in the Mayūravipina and Chāyāvana forests, O Śaṅkarī, having worshipped the Lord of the Thirty-three along with Girijā, they attained supreme liberation. || 47 ||
Having worshipped the Lord of Hālāsya, O Umā, and the Lord of the excellent rice-fields, as well as the radiant Kāśī with her long eyes,
the celestial nymphs bathe in the golden lake and dance before me and you with graceful, playful movements.

O Bhuvaneśvarī, Mārkaṇḍeya and Ghaṭodbhava, having worshipped Ghaṭahara, conquered Death in an instant; and Skanda, having worshipped Gaṇapa on Svāmigiri, [conquered him] at Dakṣiṇāvartaka, where he was struck by the trident from my foot.
Having propitiated me, the Gaṇas and the hosts of Brahmins [worship] me within the Liṅgas located there.
In me, whose abode is the swift shore (Kṣiprātīra) and who am eternally born as Mahākāla by name,
Bhṛṅgin, Nandin, Caṇḍika, the son of Bali, Paulastya, Huṇḍa, and others attained the status of Gaṇas after worshipping with meritorious deeds; though already liberated, they became my attendants.
Having propitiated me, they always praised me extensively; listen to that from me.
Thus ends the fifty-sixth chapter, titled "The Worship of the Sacred Field by the Gods," in the first part of the Śrī Śivarahasya.
Page 214) Chapter Fifty-Seven, titled "The Praise by All the Gods.
Īśvara said:
"Indeed, I have been praised here and there by the gods, the lords of the Gaṇas, and the sages."
O Daughter of the Mountain, listen attentively to that praise from me.
The gods, beginning with Viṣṇu and Brahmā, as well as my attendants, praised me, the Great God, with captivating verses and prose. || 2 ||
Viṣṇu:

I worship that river of the nectar of sacred stories which dwells within the hut of matted locks, adorned by the gathering of birds, joined with the body of the beloved of the elephant (Gajendra), graced by the beauty of the lotus-face, and flowing from the crest of the coiled hair; I bow to Maheśvara who resides upon the head of Śambhu. || 3 ||
He who wields the Candrāhasa sword, which brings an end to the bondage of the manifold hosts of Khara and the other demons;
he who, by the power of his unbroken axe, instantly knows the intentions of those such as Khara and shatters their pride as they attempt to offer him a meal.
Brahmā said:

I worship the Lord who has the deer as his emblem, who transcends the mind, transcends speech, transcends the multitude, and transcends all qualities; whose lotus-feet are honored by the coils of the king of serpents; who rests upon the stalks of blossoming lotuses tossed by the waves of the river; and who dwells within the theater of jewels. || 5 ||

I worship Śiva—the God of gods, who bestows gold, land, cattle, horses, Viṣṇu, and all other gifts; who grants enjoyment and liberation; who is established in the cave of the heart; who pervades the universe; who is manifested through power; who is praised by sublime speech; and who is lauded by the great Vedas.

I worship Rudra— the one who wears the great serpent-king as a bracelet, who is the companion of the daughter of the mountain-dweller (Pārvatī), who bears the flaming trident, who nourishes the child of the lord of sages (Śiva’s son Skanda),
who holds the tail of a deer, who bears the white triple-tilaka mark, who wears the moon, and who is clothed in the skin of the lord of elephants.

To the Lord who utters the most excellent sound of the *sāman* chant; whose circle of matted locks is fierce with the brilliance of the crescent moon; the Master who wears clear earrings upon his well-formed ears;
whose body bears a fragment of the divine moon with its unbroken rays; and who possesses a mass of matted hair shining like a cluster of Brahma’s heads—[I bow]. (8)

I worship Śiva, who performs the fierce *caṇḍatāṇḍava* dance, who is beloved by the birds of the thick clouds, who is fond of the *tuhaṇḍahuṇḍaka* [attendants], and whose arms are like the trunks of great elephants.
Indra:

I ever hold in the lotus of my heart Śiva—the destroyer of Tripura, the destroyer of Smara (Kāma), the destroyer of Bhaga, the destroyer of the sacrifice, and the ultimate destroyer of the elephant Andhaka.

Vāyu—[I praise him who is] the teacher of skill to the very dexterous, who dwells upon the back of the great bull, who is fond of the vehicle of the excellent bird, who bestows happiness and bestows glory;
(p. 215) who eclipses the great sins with his own majesty, who possesses the splendor of a multitude of great rays, and who is disregarded by the wicked. 10.
I always worship within my heart Śaṅkara, who fulfills the desires of the mind, who bestows sons, who performs the oblation, and who is most expansive.

Agni— I eternally worship Śiva, who possesses auspicious armlets and is the abode of auspiciousness; who has bestowed His own state upon the gods; who bears great majesty; who bestows prosperity and grants excellent liberation; who grants the realization that is free from existence and its causes; who wears the hide of the lordly elephant as a garment; and who bestows the full orb of the moon. 12.
Yama said:
I worship Hara, who is devoted to his true devotees, the sustainer of the earth, the bearer of blazing light, the destroyer of awakened enemies, the bestower of joy, the Great Lord;
I worship Hara, the lord of Hari, whose great bow is the mountain, and who is the goal of the world.
Sūrya said:

I ever worship the divine Sun, who withdraws the body and its enjoyments; I worship Hara and Śaṅkara, the Lord of Dancers who is higher than the highest, the tormentor of Janārdana, the one who wears the king of serpents as a crest-jewel, and the one who brings about the destruction of the great Māra.
Kubera:

I worship the Lord of Wealth, the Lord of the hosts of Gaṇas and others, the Lord of Umā, the Lord of the Bull, the Lord who is the cause of happiness for the world, the Lord of consciousness and bliss, the Lord of the Mountain, and the Lord within the heart. 15.
Candra:
[I praise] Him whose luster is like the autumn moon, who has the tail-tuft of a great bull for a chowrie, whose head is crowned with clusters of blossoms resembling large, pure trees;
He who is beloved by those free from desire, whose crest-jewel is a conch-shell fragment, the imperishable Śiva dwelling in the heart, praised by the hymns of Sukacchapa. (16)
Varuṇa said:
I worship the Lord who is superior to the superior, the beloved of the virtuous, the destroyer of what is lost, the one who dwells on the mountain, the most mighty, and likewise the eldest;
I worship Him who possesses eight forms, who is pleased by devotion, the youngest, and the sole destroyer of miseries such as suffering.

The Aśvins [saw him]— whose skin was wrinkled by the hollows of his hips, who wore the crescent moon as an ornament upon the banks of the Ganges on the slopes of the mountain frequented by the gods (Kailāsa) within his cottage of matted locks,
and whose hand held the tip of a chisel near the great stream of the Vaitaraṇī.
Vasavas:
